R0008.title: Ad Fraud
R0008.definition: Manipulating digital advertising through fake clicks or impressions, or maliciously consuming advertising resources.
R0008.description: Forging or maliciously consuming click counts or impression counts for advertising projects, causing financial losses to advertisers. This generally involves ad network fraud or malicious actions by competitors. Ad network fraud typically includes inflating click or impression counts. Competitors typically maliciously click links to exhaust advertising budgets, increasing total advertiser spend.

references.title: OWASP Automated Threat: OAT003 Ad Fraud

observables: Source IPs and device fingerprints of ad click/impression requests are highly clustered, lacking genuine user diversity
Ad clicks are decoupled from subsequent conversion behavior, with no browsing, cart-add, or ordering path after the click
Click volume on the same ad placement spikes abnormally during specific periods, far exceeding the historical baseline
Device characteristics such as User-Agent and screen resolution in ad requests show an abnormally concentrated distribution

R0008-001.title: Ad Link Hijacking
R0008-001.definition: Tampering with advertising links to change the ultimate beneficiary of the ad promotion.
R0008-001.description: Using browser plugins or applications to hijack product links or ad links, converting a user's direct product visit into a visit through an affiliate promotion link to earn commissions. Or hijacking and tampering with existing affiliate promotion links to change the ultimate beneficiary and intercept commissions.
R0008-001.influence: Financial losses to advertisers or affiliate promoters.

references.title: Software Extensions, Technique T1176 - MITRE ATT&CK

observables: Direct product links accessed by users are appended with promotional tracking parameters not triggered by the users themselves
The beneficiary of an affiliate promotion link is tampered to a party other than the original promoter
Client traffic shows a plugin or add-on program rewriting the ad destination URL
The same affiliate commission is contested by attribution claims from multiple channels, with an anomalous attribution chain

R0008-002.title: Click Fraud
R0008-002.definition: Click fraud refers to artificially generated fake click behavior through fraudulent means, typically occurring in the digital advertising space.
R0008-002.description: This behavior is designed to mislead advertising systems into recording fictitious ad click counts to obtain improper revenue or inflate ad performance metrics. Fake clicks may be generated through automated scripts, bots, click farms, and similar means rather than genuine user intent.
R0008-002.influence: May cause harm to advertisers, ad platforms, and the entire digital advertising ecosystem.

references.title: OWASP Automated Threat: OAT-003 Ad Fraud

observables: IPs, devices, and timing of ad click requests exhibit batch-script characteristics, with regular click intervals
Clicks are followed by no page-dwell, scrolling, or other genuine interaction, with a missing conversion path
The click-through rate of the same ad creative spikes abnormally within a short window, far exceeding the industry baseline
Click sources concentrate on datacenter IPs or known proxy-pool ranges, lacking residential traffic distribution

R0008-003.title: Fake App Installs
R0008-003.definition: Fake installs refer to fraudulently simulating or faking user installation behavior for an application or software to obtain false install counts or active user numbers.
R0008-003.description: Fake install methods include using automated scripts, bots, or virtual accounts to simulate large numbers of user installs, or using other technical means to generate large volumes of fake app install records in a short time. This can cause app stores and advertisers to misjudge the true value and popularity of an app.
R0008-003.influence: Financial losses to advertisers or affiliate promoters.

references.title: OWASP Automated Threat: OAT-003 Ad Fraud

observables: App install events burst within a short window, with mechanical and regular device-activation timing
Install device fingerprints, OS versions, and network environments are highly homogeneous, lacking genuine diversity
Post-install app launch behavior is anomalous, with no real usage trail before uninstall or long-term dormancy
Device association between attributed installs and ad clicks shows signs of forgery, with an unreasonable attribution chain

R0008-004.title: Impression Fraud
R0008-004.definition: Charging impression fees for ad materials that have not generated exposure or have not completed valid exposure.
R0008-004.description: For example, a media outlet places multiple display ads in the same ad slot and charges the advertiser for multiple ad impressions.

references.title: OWASP Automated Threat: OAT-003 Ad Fraud

observables: Impression-event counts for an ad placement far exceed the number of actually viewable slots, indicating multi-creative stacking billed together
Viewability metrics of impression requests are anomalous, with large volumes of exposure never entering the user's visible area
Impression volume on the same ad placement grows abnormally within a short window, without corresponding genuine user visits
Device and user features in impression logs show a high repetition rate, lacking genuine traffic diversity

R0008-005.title: Traffic Attribution Fraud
R0008-005.definition: A cheating method targeting CPA/CPS traffic that disguises organic traffic as channel traffic to obtain channel traffic commissions.
R0008-005.description: Fraudulent ad channel operators collect large amounts of device and user information, then directly send click information from different devices to the advertiser's ad click log server. If some organic traffic happens to convert within a certain time window, the activation log server records the corresponding device activation and attributes it to the fraudulent channel operator. This method of sending false information to disguise organic traffic as channel traffic can be applied at many stages, such as faking server click behavior or faking tracking code events.
R0008-005.influence: Financial losses to advertisers or affiliate promoters.

references.title: OWASP Automated Threat: OAT-003 Ad Fraud

observables: Organic conversions are attributed to a specific channel, with the attribution window aligning anomalously with click events
Device information in click logs reported by the channel shows batch-forged matches against genuinely activated devices
The channel's attribution commission share is abnormally high, far exceeding its actual traffic-driving capability
Attribution click requests cluster within a short window before conversion, exhibiting deliberate organic-traffic coverage characteristics
